Contact reach, retention ratio and the field-density measures capture a concept's position in the inter-field backbone and partly reflect a pre-onset footprint. Community count, neighbourhood novelty and ego density capture the topology of the early home-field co-occurrence neighbourhood. The OPEN index combines these into a single measure of early openness. The practical forecasting gain is small: OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ adds only +0.002 Spearman on the fresh cohort. The indicators characterise structural preconditions for broad diffusion rather than providing individually actionable forecasts. In the home-only build the weakest held-out group is Physical Sciences (PSP +0.025; Life \\& Environment +0.067, pooled +0.069); in the all-papers build Life \\& Environment is the weakest held-out group (+0.071 vs +0.181 pooled), which a boundary analysis could not explain.\n\n\n\\subsection{By what routes do concepts spread across fields?}\n\n\\label{subsec:rq2_entry}\n\\subsubsection{Experimental setup}\n\nWe test whether relatedness to the fields currently retaining a concept predicts which field it enters next, using a conditional logit on concept-year risk sets with an independent frame of 11{,}841 concepts (6{,}978 entry events in 6{,}076 informative strata)\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_MjdbXJqg-rPl/round-3/experiment-7}}. The frame excludes all concepts used in the development-set frame construction. The specification was hash-sealed on the development set before held-out scoring. Pre-registered criteria include: pooled R3 CI above zero, positive in the majority of evaluable groups, volume-matched contrast CI above zero, retained-label permutation null rejected, backbone-rewiring null rejected, and dose-response non-negative.\n\n\\subsubsection{Comparison to related work}\n\n\\citet{Hidalgo2007} showed that product-space relatedness predicts economic diversification; the minimum conditional probability defines the standard proximity. \\citet{Boschma2015} extended the principle of relatedness to regional and technological diversification, and \\citet{Fitzgerald2021} showed how regional knowledge networks shape academic localisation. Our contribution is to test whether relatedness to the set of fields currently \\emph{retaining} a concept predicts entry, beyond relatedness to the home field and conventional density measures. The key methodological distinction is that retention, not mere presence, defines the reference set.\n\n\\subsubsection{Results}\n\nOn the independent held-out frame, the retained-frontier coefficient is $d_0 = 0.322$ [0.291, 0.355] (1{,}000-draw concept bootstrap; R3 vs R2 likelihood-ratio 325.8, $p < 10^{-70}$; 3{,}162 held-out concepts). The result is positive in three of three evaluable held-out groups: Physical Sciences +0.148, Life \\& Environment +0.401, Social Sciences +0.297. Mathematics \\& Decision Sciences is null (+0.065 [$-$0.110, 0.234], 165 concepts). DerSimonian--Laird pooled $d_0$ = 0.243 [0.118, 0.368], $I^2 = 0.92$ (Table~\\ref{tab:entry}, Figure~\\ref{fig:entry}).\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Retained-frontier coefficient ($d_0$) from the conditional-logit model of field entry, by domain group and cohort. The pre-registered verdict is PARTIAL: criterion 5 (volume-matched CI $> 0$) fails.}\n\\label{tab:entry}\n\\small\n\\begin{tabular}{lccc}\n\\toprule\nModel & $d_0$ & 95\\% CI (concept bootstrap) & LR (R3 vs R2) \\\\\n\\midrule\nDevelopment set & 0.246 & [0.222, 0.271] & 365.6 \\\\\nHeld-out pooled & 0.322 & [0.291, 0.355] & 325.8 \\\\\nPhysical Sciences & 0.148 & [0.074, 0.219] & -- \\\\\nLife \\& Environment & 0.401 & [0.347, 0.458] & -- \\\\\nSocial Sciences & 0.297 & [0.245, 0.345] & -- \\\\\nMath \\& Decision Sci. & 0.065 & [$-$0.110, 0.234] & -- \\\\\n2010--2014 cohort & 0.321 & [0.292, 0.347] & -- \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe retained-frontier coefficient survives the conventional RCA density ($D_{\\text{rca}}$) and a share-weighted current presence density: adding $d_0$ after both rivals gives LR = 365.6 on DEV and 325.8 on held-out data, and on held-out data the $D_{\\text{rca}}$ coefficient falls from 0.093 to 0.022 once $d_0$ enters. All three specificity tests reject their nulls after Holm correction (retained-label permutation $p = 0.001$; backbone-rewiring $p = 0.004$; node-label $p = 0.003$).\n\nHowever, the pre-registered verdict is PARTIAL. The volume-matched contrast (comparing entry rates of retained versus entered-but-not-retained fields in the same volume cell) is null: $-$0.028 [$-$0.105, +0.046] on held-out data ($-$0.008 on DEV; Holm $p$ = 0.76). The dose response by retention age on held-out data is 0.098 / 0.075 / 0.304, which is not monotone. Under minimum-conditional-probability proximity \\citep{Hidalgo2007} instead of PMI, the held-out $d_0 = -0.021$ ($p = 0.012$), while RCA density becomes strong (LR 246). Persistence is therefore confounded with volume, and the result is backbone-specific.\n\n\\textbf{Gateway centrality.} Gateway centrality does not predict field retention: on 8{,}515 held-out episodes, the increment is effectively zero ($\\Delta$AUC $-$0.00001, 95\\% CI [$-$0.0006, +0.0003]).\n\n\\textbf{Breadth decomposition.} On 3{,}188 DEV concepts\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_MjdbXJqg-rPl/round-4/experiment-12}}, the breadth gap between the top and bottom $O_{2r}$ terciles decomposes, in the unstratified variant, as: early contact diversity 77.9\\%, frontier advance $-$4.6\\% (broad concepts gain new fields at similar rates), and retention 26.8\\%; exploration minus retention is 0.464 [0.407, 0.528]. The primary volume-stratified variant gives 76.0\\% / $-$4.5\\% / 28.5\\% and a difference of 0.431 [0.371, 0.493]. Excluding Medicine (the pre-registered variant iv), the difference is 0.633 [0.537, 0.727] on DEV, 0.492 [0.403, 0.575] on the pooled held-out groups and 0.445 [0.358, 0.527] on the 2010--2014 cohort; DerSimonian--Laird over three held-out groups gives 0.504 [0.329, 0.679] ($I^2 = 0.76$). These shares are an accounting identity for the breadth outcome, not causal effects, because breadth and contact diversity share papers.\n\n\\textbf{Diffusion trajectories.} No discrete trajectory typology passes the naming rule. DTW $k$-medoids and HMM-based clustering on state sequences give an adjusted Rand index of 0.222. PCA reveals a continuum: PC1 (38.8\\% of variance) is a breadth axis, PC2 (10.7\\%) is a keep-versus-lose axis. Early openness correlates with PC1 beyond B5 (held-out partial 0.120 for the all-papers build and 0.060 for the home-only build, $I^2 = 0$) but not positively with PC2 (DEV partial $-$0.07 to $-$0.11).\n\n\\textbf{Sequence and closure tests.} A home-prominence half-peak vs off-home take-off test finds no signal beyond the mechanical lag (DEV excess $-$0.009 [$-$0.015, $-$0.003], held-out +0.011 [0.005, 0.016]). Intersection-born concepts take off later (HR 0.47 [0.42, 0.54]). A within-concept closure test\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_MjdbXJqg-rPl/round-5/experiment-15}} is null on the development set (density PPML $b = -0.070$ [$-$0.180, 0.040]; OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ $b = +0.015$ [$-$0.038, 0.069]). On held-out fields, OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ is opposite-signed ($-$0.079 [$-$0.146, $-$0.013]), and a Sun--Abraham event study around the first home closure jump is null (DEV lag 0--2: $-$0.018 [$-$0.042, +0.004]). Early openness is a between-concept trait, not a within-concept mechanism.\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_entry_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Retained-frontier coefficient $d_0$ (log-odds of entering a field per SD of relatedness to the off-home fields that currently retain the concept) from the conditional-logit entry model (rung R3, controlling for home relatedness, field size, entered density, own gateway centrality, RCA density $D_{\\mathrm{rca}}$ and volume density $D_{\\mathrm{vol}}$), by unit. Circles with bars show point estimates with 95\\% concept-bootstrap confidence intervals. The light-blue row is the development (DEV) set used for selection. Dark-blue rows are the held-out domain groups and the 2010--14 onset cohort. The black diamond is the DerSimonian--Laird random-effects estimate pooled over the four held-out groups, and its width spans its 95\\% CI. The right column prints each estimate and interval; $n$ is the number of concepts in each unit. The dashed line marks $d_0 = 0$. $d_0$ is positive with a CI excluding zero in all three evaluable held-out groups (Physical Sciences 0.148, Life \\& Env.\\ 0.401, Social Sciences 0.297) and in the cohort (0.321). Math \\& Decision ($n = 165$, excluded as underpowered before the freeze) is null (0.065 [$-$0.110, 0.234]). The pooled estimate is 0.243 [0.118, 0.368] with high heterogeneity ($I^2 = 0.92$). The frozen verdict is nonetheless PARTIAL: the pre-registered volume-matched contrast is null, and the effect is specific to the PMI backbone.}\n  \\label{fig:entry}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\\subsubsection{Discussion of RQ2}\n\nThe retained-frontier result extends the principle of relatedness to concept adoption. The positive coefficient is large and consistent across three of three evaluable groups, but the PARTIAL verdict limits its interpretation: we cannot fully separate persistence from sustained volume as a predictor of field entry. The effect is also backbone-specific: it holds on the sparse PMI backbone but not under the standard Hidalgo proximity. The breadth decomposition shows that integrating and localised concepts differ primarily in how many fields they contact early, not in how many more fields they enter later. The null closure test and opposite-signed held-out result indicate that openness does not operate as a within-concept mechanism driving diffusion.\n\n\n\\subsection{Confound analysis}\n\\label{sec:confound}\n\nThe openness signal could be an artefact of small yearly samples or of dynamic churn. We tested four null models\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_MjdbXJqg-rPl/round-5/experiment-16}}:\n\n\\textbf{Fixed-size rarefaction.} Subsampling to 10 home papers per year retains 68\\% of the pooled association. The bias-corrected Chao estimator retains 91\\% (same-sample retention ratio 0.913).\n\n\\textbf{Within-concept permutation null.} The excess churn over a 200-draw within-concept year-label permutation null is indistinguishable from zero: excess NOVCHURN pooled PSP = +0.008 [$-$0.02, +0.03], compared to raw NOVCHURN = +0.116 [+0.09, +0.14]. The $R^2$ of raw persistence on the permutation-null mean is 0.66. What predicts breadth is a static property of the concept's home-topic partner mix.\n\n\\textbf{Degree-preserving configuration null.} Replacing raw ego density and persistence by curveball configuration $z$-scores raises OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ from +0.092 to +0.115.\n\n\\textbf{Reliability.} Split-half reliability of NOVCHURN$_{\\text{raw}}$ is 0.48. The temporal-excess variants (V2) have split-half Spearman--Brown reliability of approximately 0.01--0.05, and the planted-churn check fails. The disattenuated pooled NOVCHURN PSP is 0.178 [0.141, 0.214] (approximate, CI not independently re-derived).\n\nBecause the V2 temporal-excess measure is unreliable, the analysis cannot adjudicate temporal churn at typical sample sizes ($\\sim$10 home papers/year). The association that survives behaves like a static dispersion property. Temporal turnover is untested rather than refuted.\n\n\\textbf{Partner decomposition.} The home-only signal is carried by partners from new Leiden communities arriving through mixed-field papers: contrast $C_2$ = +0.102 [+0.069, +0.133] (Holm $p$ = 0.0025), domain Shapley $\\phi$ = +0.132 on the cohort (method = +0.012). Controlling for the share of early bridging papers halves NOVCHURN from 0.118 to 0.056.\n\n\n\\subsection{Exploratory AI-domain stage}\n\nAn exploratory retrospective atlas of 37 AI and computer science concepts was constructed from the large panel, describing the early ($t_0{-}3$ to $t_0{+}2$) co-occurrence neighbourhoods of concepts such as deep learning, convolutional neural networks, cloud computing and crowdsourcing, grouped by their later spread. This atlas is outcome-selected and retrospective; it provides qualitative context but no hypothesis-testing power.\n\n\n\\subsection{Representative case studies}\n\nSeven matched case-study pairs were drawn from the breadth decomposition analysis (Table~\\ref{tab:cases}; one pair is shown in Figure~\\ref{fig:case_study}). Each pair takes a top-quintile and a bottom-quintile OPEN$_{\\text{all}}$ concept from the same reporting group, matched on early volume, growth and onset year; in 7 of 7 pairs the high-OPEN member has the higher size-adjusted breadth. These pairs are illustration only; all are descriptive with no $p$-value.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Representative matched case-study pairs, contrasting high-openness and low-openness concepts matched on early volume and growth. All pairs are illustration; no inferential claim is made.}\n\\label{tab:cases}\n\\small\n\\begin{tabular}{lll}\n\\toprule\nHigh-OPEN concept & Low-OPEN concept & Group \\\\\n\\midrule\nGraphics processing unit & Vertical-axis wind turbine & CS+Eng \\\\\nShotgun proteomics & Image-guided radiation therapy & BGM+Med \\\\\nNanocarriers & Nanosheet & PHYS \\\\\nSoft power & Autonomous learning & SOC \\\\\nScopus & Oxygen reduction reaction & CS+Eng \\\\\nSclerostin & IgG4-related disease & BGM+Med \\\\\nUser-generated content & Mindfulness-based cognitive therapy & SOC \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_case_study_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Illustrative matched case-study pair (pair 1 of 7): graphics processing unit (GPU; onset $t_0=2008$, high early-neighbourhood openness OPEN) versus vertical-axis wind turbine (VAWT; $t_0=2009$, low OPEN). (a) Number of off-home venue fields each concept has ever entered (solid line, filled markers) and currently retains (dashed line, open markers) in each year from $t_0$ to $t_0+8$; GPU is shown in black and VAWT in grey on a shared axis. (b,~c) Topic co-occurrence ego networks over the first three years ($t_0$ to $t_0+2$, all papers). The nodes are the concept's positive-PMI neighbour topics (the concept itself is not drawn), the edges are links between those topics in the topic backbone, node area scales with the number of the concept's papers carrying the topic, and colour gives the topic's Leiden community, named by the plurality OpenAlex field. GPU's neighbourhood has 34 topics in 8 communities (density 0.30). VAWT's has 12 topics in a single Engineering community (density 0.70). The pair illustrates the openness--breadth association and is not evidence for it.}\n  \\label{fig:case_study}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\n\\subsection{Dead ends and negative results}\n\\label{sec:dead_ends}\n\nTable~\\ref{tab:deadends} lists the principal hypotheses and candidate signals that were tested and did not survive.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Principal dead ends and negative results.}\n\\label{tab:deadends}\n\\small\n\\begin{tabular}{p{4.2cm}p{2.5cm}p{5.5cm}}\n\\toprule\nHypothesis / candidate & Decisive test & Result \\\\\n\\midrule\nNaturalisation gap ($A^*_h$) & Indicator screen & Fails every clause ($-$0.006) \\\\\n$D_{\\text{ratio}}$, $F_{\\text{res}}$ & Ratio indicators & No candidate survives \\\\\nGateway landing on $O_{2r}$ & Gateway analysis & $\\Delta$AUC $-$0.00001 held-out \\\\\nH3 gateway-weighted landing & Gateway analysis & Pooled CI includes 0 [$-$0.006, 0.065] \\\\\nOrdering (central-first) & Trajectory analysis & MIXED: 32.6\\% of broad concepts; negative lead-lag; pre-trend \\\\\nTwo discrete trajectory classes & Trajectory clustering & HMM-vs-DTW ARI 0.094/0.222 \\\\\nAbandonment penalty ($d_{\\text{lost}}$) & Entry model & Specification-dependent: A1 $-$0.007, R4 +0.064, min-cp $-$0.030 \\\\\nVolume-matched retained-frontier contrast & Entry model & Null: $-$0.028 [$-$0.105, +0.046] held-out \\\\\n$O_5$ external recognition & Indicator screen & No indicator beats B5 + onset year \\\\\nRescue and relay models & Trajectory analysis & Not supported \\\\\nWithin-concept closure & Closure test & Null on DEV; opposite-signed held-out ($-$0.079) \\\\\nEarly author count for $O_3$ & Cohort replication & Non-replication on fresh cohort (+0.014) \\\\\nRetention ratio at R2/R3 & Cohort replication & Null on cohort ($-$0.043 [$-$0.116, 0.031]) \\\\\nTrait prediction ($P$-B1) & Reliability test & Fails: yearly OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ ICC 0.34--0.39 \\\\\nVocab-free Cheng reversal & Vocab-free frame & Not confirmed ($-$0.064 [$-$0.159, 0.031]) \\\\\nCo-author candidate S & Indicator screen & Computed; not confirmed for any outcome \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\n\\section{Discussion}\n\\label{sec:discussion}\n\n\\subsection{What the openness index captures}\n\nThe OPEN index captures the degree to which a concept's early neighbourhood acquires partners from diverse communities rather than reinforcing existing ones. The signal is not demonstrably temporal turnover but a static topical-dispersion property. A within-concept permutation null absorbs the year-to-year component, yet the association persists: concepts whose home-field co-occurrence partners span many communities tend to reach more fields later. This is consistent with \\citeauthor{March1991}'s (\\citeyear{March1991}) exploration--exploitation distinction at the concept level. However, the within-concept closure test is null on DEV and opposite-signed on held-out fields, indicating that openness operates as a between-concept trait rather than as a within-concept causal mechanism.\n\nThe home-only signal (OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$) is marginal. The stronger OPEN$_{\\text{all}}$ signal is partly mechanically coupled: early off-home papers that enter the ego network are a subset of the papers that determine the outcome. OPEN$_{\\text{sizematch}}$ equalises paper counts but still includes off-home papers, so it does not remove the coupling; it lies between the two builds (OPEN$_{\\text{sizematch}}$ minus OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ +0.053 [$-$0.015, +0.117]).\n\n\\subsection{Reconciling consistency and breadth}\n\n\\citet{Cheng2023} found that ideational consistency predicts a concept becoming ``core.'' We replicate their result for volume (+53\\%/SD) but show that it is almost entirely a current-size effect (+1.3\\%/SD once current volume is controlled) and that, net of the popularity baseline, the same property predicts \\emph{narrower} cross-field reach. The reversal holds in all five field groups ($I^2 = 0$) and on the 2015--2017 cohort, all selection data, but it is not confirmed on the vocabulary-free frame ($-0.064$, CI includes zero). The features predictive of local consolidation and growth are distinct from, and partly opposed to, the features predictive of broad disciplinary spread.\n\n\\subsection{The retained-frontier claim}\n\nThe field-entry result ($d_0 = 0.322$ on the independent frame) extends the principle of relatedness from economic geography \\citep{Hidalgo2007,Boschma2015} to concept adoption. The result is PARTIAL: the volume-matched contrast is null, and the effect is backbone-specific (it reverses under minimum-conditional-probability proximity). What survives is a PMI-backbone relative-odds effect that cannot be separated from volume. The $I^2$ of 0.92 indicates substantial cross-domain heterogeneity, with Life \\& Environment showing the strongest signal and Mathematics \\& Decision Sciences null.\n\n\\subsection{Limitations}\n\n\\textbf{Effect size.} The OPEN--breadth association is modest. OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ adds no forecasting gain over B5 (+0.002 [$-$0.003, +0.008]).\n\n\\textbf{Measurement noise.} Split-half reliability of OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ is 0.49. The temporal-excess variants have split-half reliability below 0.05, so temporal versus static dispersion cannot be resolved at available sample sizes.\n\n\\textbf{Vocabulary bias.} The legacy OpenAlex concept vocabulary is survivor-selected. Frame~N is small (636 concepts) with pre-unseal power of 0.47.\n\n\\textbf{Coupling.} About half of the OPEN$_{\\text{all}}$ signal is mechanical coupling between the ego-network construction (which uses off-home papers) and the breadth outcome. OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ is free of this coupling but marginal.\n\n\\textbf{Domain heterogeneity.} The home-only OPEN signal is weakest in Physical Sciences (PSP +0.025); in the all-papers build Life \\& Environment is weakest (+0.071). The retained-field relatedness $I^2$ is 0.92.\n\n\\textbf{Not causal.} Early ego-network openness could reflect a concept's intrinsic generality, the diversity of the research community around it, or the breadth of the problems it addresses.\n\n\\textbf{Prior unsealing.} Held-out outcomes were previously unsealed by two earlier experiments in the same project, so the indicator-screen held-out results are robustness checks.\n\n\n\\section{Conclusions}\n\\label{sec:conclusions}\n\nWe screened 53 early temporal network indicators for predicting the cross-disciplinary breadth of new scientific concepts, using 12{,}499 concepts from the OpenAlex corpus with held-out validation and a fresh cohort confirmation. Seven indicators are confirmed; from the ego-network family we build the OPEN index, which captures topical non-redundancy in a concept's early co-occurrence neighbourhood and has a small association with breadth (pooled +0.069) but no forecasting gain. The signal is a static between-concept trait; temporal turnover could not be tested at available sample sizes. Early openness is associated with breadth; early consolidation goes with volume even after controlling for current size (+0.094 [0.007, 0.186] on the vocabulary-free frame) and, net of volume, with narrower breadth on selection data (not confirmed on the vocabulary-free frame). Concepts spread next to fields related to those currently retaining them, but the pre-registered verdict is PARTIAL: persistence and volume are confounded, and the effect is backbone-specific.\n\n\n\\section*{Declarations}\n\n\\subsection*{Availability of data and materials}\n\\begin{sloppypar}\nThe study uses the publicly available OpenAlex bulk snapshot (2026-09-23). Analysis code is available at\n\\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_MjdbXJqg-rPl};\nindividual experiment folders are linked in the paper's footnotes. Concept frames and indicator matrices are available from the corresponding author upon request.\n\\end{sloppypar}\n\n\\subsection*{Competing interests}\nThe authors declare no competing interests.\n\n\\subsection*{Funding}\nNot applicable.\n\n\\subsection*{Authors' contributions}\nAll authors contributed to the study design, analysis and manuscript preparation.\n\n\\subsection*{Acknowledgements}\nNot applicable.\n\n\\bibliographystyle{plainnat}\n\\bibliography{references}\n\n\\end{document}\n", "numLines": 440, "startLine": 1, "totalLines": 440}}

def rank(a):
  idx=sorted(range(len(a)),key=lambda i:a[i]); r=[0]*len(a); i=0
  while i<len(a):
    j=i
    while j+1<len(a) and a[idx[j+1]]==a[idx[i]]: j+=1
    for k in range(i,j+1): r[idx[k]]=(i+j)/2+1
    i=j+1
  return r
def sp(x,y):
  rx,ry=rank(x),rank(y); n=len(x); mx=sum(rx)/n; my=sum(ry)/n
  num=sum((a-mx)*(b-my) for a,b in zip(rx,ry)); import math
  return num/math.sqrt(sum((a-mx)**2 for a in rx)*sum((b-my)**2 for b in ry))

    if r["body"] not in bodies:
        continue
    row = {"body": r["body"], "feature": r["feature"], "status": r["status"], "onsets": r.get("onsets"),
           "n_body": r.get("n_body_rows"), "placebo_p95": r["placebo"]["p95_abs_psp"] if r.get("placebo") else None}

        if r.get(k):
            row[k] = {"psp": r[k]["psp"], "ci": r[k]["ci"], "n": r[k]["n"]}
    rows.append(row)
pools = {}
for key, p in es["pools"].items():
    ns = p["nonselection"]

                  "sign": p["sign_agreement_nonselection"], "bodies": p["nonselection_bodies"],
                  "sel": p["selection_body_estimate"], "shrink": p["shrinkage_ratio_selection_over_nonselection"]}
dump("synthesis", {"rows": rows, "pools": pools},

.controls{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:12px 20px;align-items:flex-end;margin:0 0 12px}
fieldset{border:0;margin:0;padding:0;min-width:0}
legend,.lab{font-size:14px;color:var(--ink3);font-weight:600;margin-bottom:4px;padding:0;display:block}
.seg{display:inline-flex;border:1px solid var(--muted);border-radius:6px;overflow:hidden;flex-wrap:wrap}
.seg label{position:relative;display:inline-flex}
.seg input{position:absolute;opacity:0;width:1px;height:1px}
.seg span{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;min-height:40px;min-width:40px;padding:0 12px;font-size:15px;cursor:pointer;background:#fff;color:var(--ink2);border-right:1px solid var(--rule)}
.seg label:last-child span{border-right:0}
.seg input:checked+span{background:var(--accent);color:#fff;font-weight:600}
.seg input:focus-visible+span{outline:3px solid var(--focus);outline-offset:-3px}
.chk{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;min-height:40px;font-size:15px;cursor:pointer;color:var(--ink2)}
.chk input{width:20px;height:20px;accent-color:var(--accent)}
select,input[type=search]{font:inherit;font-size:15px;min-height:40px;padding:6px 10px;border:1px solid var(--muted);border-radius:6px;background:#fff;color:var(--ink);max-width:100%}
input[type=range]{width:min(320px,100%);min-height:40px;accent-color:var(--accent)}
.chart{position:relative;width:100%}
.chart svg{display:block;width:100%;overflow:visible}
.chart svg text{font-family:var(--font);fill:var(--ink2)}
.legend{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:6px 16px;font-size:14px;color:var(--ink2);margin:6px 0 0;padding:0;list-style:none}
.legend li{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:6px}
.sw{display:inline-block;width:14px;height:14px;border-radius:2px}
.take{border-left:4px solid var(--accent);background:var(--accent-soft);padding:10px 14px;margin:14px 0 0;border-radius:0 6px 6px 0;font-size:17px;max-width:75ch}
.take::before{content:"Takeaway. ";font-weight:700}
.note{font-size:15px;color:var(--ink3);max-width:75ch}
.tip{position:absolute;z-index:30;pointer-events:none;background:#fff;border:1px solid var(--ink3);border-radius:6px;padding:8px 10px;font-size:14px;line-height:1.4;box-shadow:0 4px 14px rgba(0,0,0,.12);max-width:280px;display:none}
.tip b{display:block;margin-bottom:2px}
.mark{cursor:pointer}
.mark:focus{outline:none}
.mark:focus-visible .hit,.mark.hot .hit{stroke:var(--focus);stroke-width:2.5;fill:rgba(242,169,0,.10)}
.term{font:inherit;color:inherit;background:none;border:0;padding:0 1px;border-bottom:1.5px dotted var(--accent);cursor:help;min-height:auto}
.term:hover,.term[aria-expanded="true"]{background:var(--accent-soft)}
#termtip{position:absolute;z-index:50;max-width:320px;background:var(--ink);color:#fff;font-size:15px;line-height:1.45;padding:10px 12px;border-radius:6px;display:none;box-shadow:0 6px 18px rgba(0,0,0,.25)}
#termtip b{color:#ffd98a}
/* stepper */
.steps{list-style:none;margin:10px 0 0;padding:0;display:flex;gap:6px;flex-wrap:wrap}
.steps button{min-width:44px;min-height:44px;border-radius:22px;border:1px solid var(--muted);background:#fff;color:var(--ink2);font:inherit;font-size:15px;padding:0 14px;cursor:pointer}
.steps button[aria-current="step"]{background:var(--accent);border-color:var(--accent);color:#fff;font-weight:600}
.stepnav{display:flex;gap:10px;margin-top:14px;align-items:center;flex-wrap:wrap}
.btn[disabled]{opacity:.4;cursor:not-allowed}
.io{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(2,minmax(0,1fr));gap:12px;margin:12px 0}
@media (max-width:640px){.io{grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr)}}
.io div{background:var(--bg);border:1px solid var(--rule);border-radius:8px;padding:10px 12px;font-size:16px}
.io h4{margin:0 0 4px;font-size:13px;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.05em;color:var(--ink3)}
table{border-collapse:collapse;font-size:15px;width:100%}
th,td{text-align:left;padding:6px 8px;border-bottom:1px solid var(--rule);vertical-align:top}
th{color:var(--ink3);font-weight:600;font-size:14px}
td.n,th.n{text-align:right;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}
.tscroll{overflow-x:auto;max-width:100%}
figure{margin:18px 0}
figure img{max-width:100%;height:auto;display:block;border:1px solid var(--rule);border-radius:6px;background:#fff}
figcaption{font-size:15px;color:var(--ink2);margin-top:8px;max-width:80ch}
/* browser */
.browser{display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(0,4fr) minmax(0,7fr);gap:18px}
@media (max-width:900px){.browser{grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr)}}
.clist{list-style:none;margin:0;padding:0;max-height:520px;overflow-y:auto;border:1px solid var(--rule);border-radius:8px;background:#fff}
.clist button{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;gap:8px;width:100%;text-align:left;min-height:44px;padding:6px 10px;border:0;border-bottom:1px solid var(--grid);background:#fff;font:inherit;font-size:15px;color:var(--ink);cursor:pointer}
.clist button[aria-pressed="true"]{background:var(--accent-soft);box-shadow:inset 4px 0 0 var(--accent)}
.clist .meta{color:var(--ink3);font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;white-space:nowrap}
.stats{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:10px;margin:10px 0}
.stat{background:#fff;border:1px solid var(--rule);border-radius:8px;padding:8px 12px;min-width:120px}
.stat .v{font-size:22px;font-weight:700;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}
.stat .k{font-size:13px;color:var(--ink3)}
[role=tablist]{display:flex;gap:6px;flex-wrap:wrap;border-bottom:1px solid var(--rule);margin:8px 0 14px}
[role=tab]{min-height:44px;padding:0 14px;border:1px solid var(--rule);border-bottom:0;border-radius:6px 6px 0 0;background:var(--muted-soft);font:inherit;font-size:15px;color:var(--ink2);cursor:pointer}
[role=tab][aria-selected="true"]{background:#fff;color:var(--accent);font-weight:600;box-shadow:inset 0 3px 0 var(--accent)}
.limits li{margin-bottom:8px}
footer{margin-top:48px;padding:36px 0 60px;border-top:1px solid var(--rule);background:var(--panel)}
dl.gloss{display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr);gap:4px}
dl.gloss dt{font-weight:700;margin-top:10px}
dl.gloss dd{margin:0;color:var(--ink2);max-width:80ch}
.prov li{margin-bottom:6px;font-size:16px}
code{font-size:.9em;background:var(--muted-soft);padding:1px 4px;border-radius:3px}
.pill{display:inline-block;font-size:13px;padding:1px 8px;border-radius:10px;background:var(--muted-soft);color:var(--ink2)}
.pill.ok{background:#e1f2e9;color:var(--ok)} .pill.bad{background:var(--warn-soft);color:var(--warn)}
</style>
</head>
<body>
<a class="skip" href="#main">Skip to main content</a>
<header class="hero">
  <div class="wrap">
    <p class="kicker">Interactive companion to the paper</p>
    <h1>Early co-occurrence network openness is associated with cross-disciplinary concept breadth: evidence from 12,499 scientific concepts</h1>
    <p class="byline">AI Inventor</p>
    <div class="links">
      <a class="btn primary" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them@fork/run_MjdbXJqg-rPl/paper.pdf">Read the paper (PDF)</a>
      <a class="btn" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them@fork/run_MjdbXJqg-rPl/report.pdf">Read the full research report</a>
      <a class="btn" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_MjdbXJqg-rPl">Code repository</a>
    </div>
  </div>
</header>
<nav class="toc" aria-label="Sections">
  <ul>
    <li><a href="#finding">The finding</a></li>
    <li><a href="#how">How it works</a></li>
    <li><a href="#evidence">Explore the evidence</a></li>
    <li><a href="#try">Try it</a></li>
    <li><a href="#fails">Where it fails</a></li>
    <li><a href="#notes">Links and glossary</a></li>
  </ul>
</nav>
<main id="main" tabindex="-1">

<section id="finding" aria-labelledby="h-finding">
<div class="wrap">
  <h2 id="h-finding">The finding</h2>
  <div class="grid2">
    <div>
      <p class="q"><strong>Question.</strong> When a new scientific concept appears, does the shape of its early <button class="term" data-term="ego">co-occurrence neighbourhood</button> tell us how broadly it will spread across fields six to eight years later, beyond what its early popularity already says?</p>
      <p class="prose"><strong>Answer.</strong> A little, and consistently. Concepts whose home-field neighbours span many topic communities and keep changing reach more venue fields later. The <button class="term" data-term="open">OPEN index</button>, built from six such network measures, has a small positive <button class="term" data-term="psp">partial Spearman</button> with <button class="term" data-term="o2r">rarefied breadth</button> after controlling for the <button class="term" data-term="b5">B5 popularity baseline</button>. The sign is the same in every body of data tested, but the effect is too small to improve a forecast.</p>
      <p class="bignum" id="bignum" aria-describedby="bigcap">+0.069</p>
      <p class="bigcap" id="bigcap">Pooled partial Spearman of OPEN<sub>home</sub> with breadth across six <button class="term" data-term="nonsel">non-selection bodies</button> at <button class="term" data-term="rung">ladder rung R2</button>.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="card">
      <h3 style="margin-top:0">Does it hold in every body of data?</h3>
      <div class="controls">
        <fieldset><legend>Index</legend>
          <div class="seg" id="f-feat">
            <label><input type="radio" name="feat" value="OPEN_home" checked><span>OPEN<sub>home</sub></span></label>
            <label><input type="radio" name="feat" value="NOVCHURN_home"><span>NOVCHURN<sub>home</sub></span></label>
          </div></fieldset>
        <fieldset><legend>Control rung</legend>
          <div class="seg" id="f-rung">
            <label><input type="radio" name="rung" value="R0"><span>R0</span></label>
            <label><input type="radio" name="rung" value="R2" checked><span>R2</span></label>
            <label><input type="radio" name="rung" value="R3"><span>R3</span></label>
          </div></fieldset>
        <label class="chk"><input type="checkbox" id="f-dev" checked> Show DEV selection body</label>
        <label class="chk"><input type="checkbox" id="f-plac" checked> Show shuffled-outcome band</label>
      </div>
      <div class="chart" id="c-forest"><svg id="s-forest" role="group" aria-label="Forest plot of partial Spearman by body"></svg><div class="tip" role="status"></div></div>
      <ul class="legend" aria-label="Legend">
        <li><span class="sw" style="background:var(--accent)"></span>Body estimate, 95% CI</li>
        <li><span class="sw" style="background:#111;transform:rotate(45deg) scale(.8)"></span>DerSimonian–Laird pool</li>
        <li><span class="sw" style="background:var(--muted)"></span>DEV selection body (not pooled)</li>
        <li><span class="sw" style="background:var(--muted-soft);border:1px solid var(--rule)"></span>Shuffled-outcome 95th percentile, |ρ| (baseline)</li>
      </ul>
      <p class="take" id="t-finding" aria-live="polite"></p>
      <p class="note">Shuffled-outcome bands come from 200 within-body outcome permutations at R2 and are drawn for every rung as a reference for chance-level size. Point at or tab to a row for its full record.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
</section>

<section id="how" aria-labelledby="h-how">
<div class="wrap">
  <h2 id="h-how">How it works</h2>
  <p class="q"><strong>What happens to one concept on its way to a number?</strong> The study grounds 12,499 concepts in the OpenAlex snapshot, measures each one's first three years, and follows it to years six to eight. The overview shows the whole design; the stepper below walks one real concept, graphics processing unit (GPU), through each stage beside its matched low-openness partner, vertical-axis wind turbine (VAWT).</p>
  <figure>
    <img src="figures/fig_overview_v0.jpg" alt="Study design flow: OpenAlex snapshot of 476M works, concept identification keeping 12,499 grounded concepts, a panel split into DEV 4,771, held-out 3,372, cohort 4,356 and a fresh 2015-2017 cohort of 1,443, computation of 53 indicators in six families, and two analyses: RQ1 screen and validate (7 confirmed, OPEN pooled +0.069) and RQ2 conditional logit (11,841 concepts, d0 = 0.322, verdict PARTIAL)." width="1900" height="573" loading="lazy">
    <figcaption>Overview of the study design, read left to right. The OpenAlex snapshot (476M works, 129.4M base works 1995–2022) is title-matched against 56,643 legacy concepts, and Aho–Corasick matching plus an LLM precision gate keeps 12,499 grounded concepts. The panel split assigns these to a development set (DEV 4,771), four held-out domain groups (3,372) and a 2010–2014 onset cohort (4,356); a fresh 2015–2017 cohort (1,443) comes from a separate scan. 53 early indicators in six families are computed in the t<sub>0</sub> to t<sub>0</sub>+2 window, screened on DEV and validated on held-out groups (RQ1). Separately, a conditional-logit entry model is fitted on an independent frame of 11,841 concepts (RQ2).</figcaption>
  </figure>
  <div class="card" id="stepper" aria-labelledby="h-step">
    <h3 id="h-step" style="margin-top:0">One concept through the pipeline</h3>
    <div class="chart" id="c-pipe"><svg id="s-pipe" role="img" aria-label="Pipeline diagram with six stages; the current stage is highlighted"></svg></div>
    <ol class="steps" id="step-markers" aria-label="Stages"></ol>
    <p class="sr-only" id="step-live" aria-live="polite"></p>
    <div id="step-body"></div>
    <div class="stepnav">
      <button class="btn" id="step-prev" type="button">Previous stage</button>
      <button class="btn" id="step-next" type="button">Next stage</button>
      <span class="note">Left and right arrow keys also move between stages.</span>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
</section>

<section id="evidence" aria-labelledby="h-evidence">
<div class="wrap">
  <h2 id="h-evidence">Explore the evidence</h2>

  <h3>Which early signals survive held-out validation?</h3>
  <p class="q">Ten indicators were chosen on the development set and scored once on four held-out field groups and two cohort splits. Pick a unit to see whether each indicator's partial Spearman with breadth holds there.</p>
  <div class="card">
    <div class="controls">
      <div><label class="lab" for="f-unit">Unit</label>
        <select id="f-unit"></select></div>
    </div>
    <div class="chart" id="c-screen"><svg id="s-screen" role="group" aria-label="Indicator screen forest plot"></svg><div class="tip" role="status"></div></div>
    <ul class="legend">
      <li><span class="sw" style="background:var(--accent)"></span>Confirmed on held-out (Holm p &lt; 0.05, CI excludes zero)</li>
      <li><span class="sw" style="background:var(--muted)"></span>Not confirmed</li>
    </ul>
    <p class="take" id="t-screen" aria-live="polite"></p>
    <h4>Do the indicators add forecasting power over the baseline?</h4>
    <div class="chart" id="c-learned"><svg id="s-learned" role="group" aria-label="Bar chart of Spearman with breadth for baseline and learned models"></svg><div class="tip" role="status"></div></div>
    <p class="take" id="t-learned"></p>
  </div>

  <h3>What does openness look like for a single concept?</h3>
  <p class="q">The fresh 2015–2017 cohort was never used to choose the index. Each record below holds a concept's early inputs, a frozen B5-only forecast of its breadth, a frozen B5 + OPEN<sub>home</sub> forecast, and the breadth it actually reached. Filter, search and sort, then select a concept.</p>
  <div class="card">
    <div class="controls">
      <div><label class="lab" for="b-search">Search concepts</label><input type="search" id="b-search" placeholder="e.g. homology"></div>
      <div><label class="lab" for="b-group">Home group</label><select id="b-group"></select></div>
      <div><label class="lab" for="b-scope">Records</label><select id="b-scope">
        <option value="full">With outcome and both forecasts</option>
        <option value="obs">With observed breadth</option>
        <option value="all">All cohort concepts</option></select></div>
      <div><label class="lab" for="b-sort">Sort by</label><select id="b-sort">
        <option value="open">OPEN<sub>home</sub>, high to low</option>
        <option value="excess">Breadth beyond B5 forecast</option>
        <option value="obs">Observed breadth</option>
        <option value="name">Name</option></select></div>
      <label class="chk"><input type="checkbox" id="b-worse"> Only where OPEN moved the forecast away from the observed value</label>
    </div>
    <div class="stats" id="b-stats" aria-live="polite"></div>
    <div class="browser">
      <div>
        <p class="note" id="b-count" style="margin:0 0 6px"></p>
        <ul class="clist" id="b-list" aria-label="Concepts"></ul>
        <button class="btn" id="b-more" type="button" style="margin-top:8px">Show 50 more</button>
      </div>
      <div>
        <div id="b-detail"></div>
        <h4>All concepts in view: openness against breadth beyond the B5 forecast</h4>
        <div class="chart" id="c-scatter"><svg id="s-scatter" tabindex="0" role="img" aria-label="Scatter plot. Use left and right arrow keys to move between concepts."></svg><div class="tip" role="status"></div></div>
        <ul class="legend"><li><span class="sw" style="background:var(--accent);border-radius:7px"></span>Concept in view</li><li><span class="sw" style="background:var(--warn);border-radius:7px"></span>Selected concept</li><li><span class="sw" style="background:var(--muted);height:2px"></span>Zero: breadth exactly as B5 forecast</li></ul>
      </div>
    </div>
    <p class="take" id="t-browser" aria-live="polite"></p>
    <p class="note">Spearman values in the tiles are computed live over the concepts in view. With no filter they reproduce the recorded 0.768 (B5) and 0.770 (B5 + OPEN<sub>home</sub>) on 573 concepts.</p>
  </div>
</div>
</section>

<section id="try" aria-labelledby="h-try">
<div class="wrap">
  <h2 id="h-try">Try it</h2>
  <h3>Compute OPEN yourself</h3>
  <p class="q">OPEN is simple enough to run here: each component is <button class="term" data-term="z">z-scored</button> with constants frozen on the 12,499-concept frame, signed, and averaged. Pick a concept from the seven matched case pairs, choose a build, and switch components off to see what carries the score.</p>
  <div class="card">
    <div class="controls">
      <div><label class="lab" for="o-concept">Concept</label><select id="o-concept"></select></div>
      <fieldset><legend>Build</legend><div class="seg" id="o-build">
        <label><input type="radio" name="build" value="home" checked><span>Home only</span></label>
        <label><input type="radio" name="build" value="all"><span>All papers</span></label>
        <label><input type="radio" name="build" value="size"><span>Size-matched</span></label></div></fieldset>
    </div>
    <fieldset><legend>Components included</legend><div class="controls" id="o-comps"></div></fieldset>
    <div class="tscroll"><table id="o-table"></table></div>
    <div class="chart" id="c-open"><svg id="s-open" role="group" aria-label="Signed z-score of each OPEN component"></svg><div class="tip" role="status"></div></div>
    <p class="take" id="t-open" aria-live="polite"></p>
  </div>

  <h3>What if we split the cohort at an openness threshold?</h3>
  <p class="q">Move the threshold over the recorded OPEN<sub>home</sub> scores of the 573 cohort concepts that have both forecasts and an outcome. The chart recomputes how far concepts on each side landed from their B5 forecast.</p>
  <div class="card">
    <div class="controls">
      <div><label class="lab" for="w-pct">Threshold percentile of OPEN<sub>home</sub>: <output id="w-out" for="w-pct"></output></label>
      <input type="range" id="w-pct" min="10" max="90" step="5" value="50"></div>
    </div>
    <div class="chart" id="c-whatif"><svg id="s-whatif" role="group" aria-label="Mean breadth beyond B5 forecast above and below the threshold"></svg><div class="tip" role="status"></div></div>
    <p class="take" id="t-whatif" aria-live="polite"></p>
    <p class="note">Breadth beyond forecast = observed O<sub>2r</sub> (m = 50) minus the frozen B5-only forecast, in venue fields. This is a descriptive split of recorded values, not the paper's partial Spearman.</p>
  </div>
</div>
</section>

<section id="fails" aria-labelledby="h-fails">
<div class="wrap">
  <h2 id="h-fails">Where it fails</h2>
  <p class="q">Three places where the evidence stops short: the churn signal under noise controls, the retained-frontier entry model, and individual concepts that openness mis-forecasts.</p>
  <div class="card">
    <div role="tablist" aria-label="Failure views" id="fail-tabs">
      <button role="tab" id="tab-noise" aria-controls="p-noise" aria-selected="true">Churn under noise controls</button>
      <button role="tab" id="tab-entry" aria-controls="p-entry" aria-selected="false" tabindex="-1">Retained-frontier entry</button>
      <button role="tab" id="tab-miss" aria-controls="p-miss" aria-selected="false" tabindex="-1">Mis-forecast concepts</button>
    </div>
    <div role="tabpanel" id="p-noise" aria-labelledby="tab-noise">
      <p class="prose">Is the <button class="term" data-term="novchurn">NOVCHURN</button> signal real turnover, or an artefact of thin yearly samples? Each row re-scores the pooled association after one noise control.</p>
      <div class="chart" id="c-noise"><svg id="s-noise" role="group" aria-label="Partial Spearman of NOVCHURN variants"></svg><div class="tip" role="status"></div></div>
      <p class="take" id="t-noise"></p>
    </div>
    <div role="tabpanel" id="p-entry" aria-labelledby="tab-entry" hidden>
      <p class="prose">Do concepts enter next the fields related to the ones that <button class="term" data-term="retain">currently retain</button> them? The <button class="term" data-term="d0">retained-frontier coefficient d<sub>0</sub></button> is positive, but switch on the checks the pre-registration required.</p>
      <label class="chk"><input type="checkbox" id="e-checks"> Show the specificity checks that failed</label>
      <div class="chart" id="c-entry"><svg id="s-entry" role="group" aria-label="Retained-frontier coefficient by unit"></svg><div class="tip" role="status"></div></div>
      <p class="take" id="t-entry" aria-live="polite"></p>
    </div>
    <div role="tabpanel" id="p-miss" aria-labelledby="tab-miss" hidden>
      <p class="prose" id="miss-text"></p>
      <button class="btn" id="miss-go" type="button">Show these concepts in the browser</button>
      <div class="chart" id="c-miss"><svg id="s-miss" role="group" aria-label="Distribution of forecast change from adding OPEN"></svg><div class="tip" role="status"></div></div>
      <p class="take" id="t-miss"></p>
    </div>
  </div>
  <h3>What the paper does not show</h3>
  <ul class="limits prose">
    <li><strong>No forecasting gain.</strong> OPEN<sub>home</sub> adds no forecasting gain over B5 (+0.002 [−0.003, +0.008]). The association is modest.</li>
    <li><strong>Not causal.</strong> Early openness could reflect a concept's intrinsic generality, the diversity of the research community around it, or the breadth of the problems it addresses. A within-concept closure test is null on DEV and opposite-signed on held-out fields (−0.079), so openness behaves as a between-concept trait.</li>
    <li><strong>Temporal turnover is untested, not refuted.</strong> The temporal-excess variants have split-half reliability below 0.05, so static dispersion and temporal churn cannot be separated at about 10 home papers per year.</li>
    <li><strong>Mechanical coupling.</strong> About half of the OPEN<sub>all</sub> signal is coupling between off-home papers in the ego network and the breadth outcome. OPEN<sub>home</sub> is free of it but marginal: on the fresh cohort its DerSimonian–Laird interval includes zero (+0.083 [−0.007, +0.173]).</li>
    <li><strong>Prior unsealing.</strong> Held-out outcomes were read by earlier experiments in the same project, so the pool is descriptive rather than confirmatory. Only the 2015–2017 cohort was never used before.</li>
    <li><strong>Vocabulary bias.</strong> The legacy concept vocabulary is survivor-selected; the vocabulary-free frame is small (636 concepts, pre-unseal power 0.47) and its verdict is partial.</li>
    <li><strong>Retained-frontier entry is PARTIAL.</strong> Persistence and volume stay confounded, and the effect is specific to the PMI backbone.</li>
  </ul>
</div>
</section>
</main>

<script>
"use strict";
(function(){
const get = id => JSON.parse(document.getElementById(id).textContent).data;
const SYN = get('data-synthesis'), SCR = get('data-screen'), COH = get('data-cohort'),
      CASES = get('data-cases'), ENTRY = get('data-entry'), NOISE = get('data-noise');
const $ = s => document.querySelector(s);
const NS = 'http://www.w3.org/2000/svg';
const MINUS = '−';
const reduceMotion = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;
function el(tag, attrs, parent){ const e = document.createElementNS(NS, tag); if (attrs) for (const k in attrs) e.setAttribute(k, attrs[k]); if (parent) parent.appendChild(e); return e; }
function txt(parent, x, y, s, attrs){ const t = el('text', Object.assign({x: x, y: y}, attrs || {}), parent); t.textContent = s; return t; }
function f(x, d, sign){ if (d === undefined) d = 3; if (sign === undefined) sign = true; if (x === null || x === undefined || isNaN(x)) return 'n/a';
  const s = Math.abs(x).toFixed(d); if (Number(s) === 0) return s; return (x < 0 ? MINUS : (sign ? '+' : '')) + s; }
function fci(a, d, sign){ return '[' + f(a[0], d, sign) + ', ' + f(a[1], d, sign) + ']'; }
function esc(s){ return String(s).replace(/[&<>"]/g, c => ({'&':'&amp;','<':'&lt;','>':'&gt;','"':'&quot;'}[c])); }
const CSSV = n => getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue(n).trim();
const C = { accent: CSSV('--accent'), muted: CSSV('--muted'), mutedSoft: CSSV('--muted-soft'), ink: CSSV('--ink'), ink2: CSSV('--ink2'), grid: CSSV('--grid'), rule: CSSV('--rule'), warn: CSSV('--warn') };
// text measurement
const mSvg = el('svg', {width: 0, height: 0, style: 'position:absolute;left:-9999px;top:0;visibility:hidden'}); document.body.appendChild(mSvg);
const mText = el('text', {x: 0, y: 0, style: 'font-family:' + CSSV('--font')}, mSvg);
function measure(s, fs, weight){ mText.setAttribute('font-size', fs); mText.setAttribute('font-weight', weight || 400); mText.textContent = s; return mText.getComputedTextLength(); }
function niceTicks(lo, hi, n){ const span = hi - lo; const step0 = span / Math.max(1, n); const mag = Math.pow(10, Math.floor(Math.log10(step0))); const e = step0 / mag;
  const step = (e >= 7.5 ? 10 : e >= 3.5 ? 5 : e >= 1.5 ? 2 : 1) * mag; const out = [];
  for (let v = Math.ceil(lo / step - 1e-9) * step; v <= hi + 1e-9; v += step) out.push(Number(v.toFixed(10))); return out; }
function tickFmt(v, step){ const d = step >= 1 ? 0 : step >= 0.1 ? 1 : step >= 0.01 ? 2 : 3; return f(v, d, false); }

// shared chart tooltip behaviour
function bindMark(g, chartDiv, html){
  const tip = chartDiv.querySelector('.tip');
  const show = () => { chartDiv.querySelectorAll('.mark.hot').forEach(m => m.classList.remove('hot')); g.classList.add('hot'); tip.innerHTML = html; tip.style.display = 'block';
    const cb = chartDiv.getBoundingClientRect(), gb = g.getBoundingClientRect();
    let left = gb.left - cb.left + gb.width / 2 - tip.offsetWidth / 2; left = Math.max(0, Math.min(left, cb.width - tip.offsetWidth));
    let top = gb.top - cb.top - tip.offsetHeight - 8; if (top < 0) top = gb.bottom - cb.top + 8; tip.style.left = left + 'px'; tip.style.top = top + 'px'; };
  const hide = () => { g.classList.remove('hot'); tip.style.display = 'none'; };
  g.addEventListener('mouseenter', show); g.addEventListener('focus', show); g.addEventListener('click', e => { e.stopPropagation(); show(); });
  g.addEventListener('mouseleave', hide); g.addEventListener('blur', hide);
}
document.addEventListener('click', () => { document.querySelectorAll('.chart .tip').forEach(t => { t.style.display = 'none'; }); document.querySelectorAll('.mark.hot').forEach(m => m.classList.remove('hot')); });

/* ---------- generic forest plot ---------- */
function forest(svgId, rows, o){
  const svg = document.getElementById(svgId), div = svg.parentNode; svg.innerHTML = '';
  const W = Math.max(280, div.clientWidth); const fs = W < 480 ? 12 : 13;
  const labelW = Math.max.apply(null, rows.map(r => measure(r.label, fs, r.bold ? 700 : 400))) + 8;
  const showVals = W >= 600;
  const valTexts = rows.map(r => showVals ? r.valueText : r.shortText);
  const valW = Math.max.apply(null, valTexts.map(t => measure(t, fs))) + 12;
  const rowH = 30, top = 8, bottom = 46;
  const sepIdx = rows.findIndex(r => r.sep);
  const H = top + rows.length * rowH + (sepIdx >= 0 ? 10 : 0) + bottom;
  svg.setAttribute('viewBox', '0 0 ' + W + ' ' + H); svg.setAttribute('height', H);
  const x0 = labelW + 10, x1 = W - valW - 8;
  let lo = Math.min(0, ...rows.map(r => (r.lo ?? r.est)), ...(rows.map(r => r.band ? -r.band : 0)));
  let hi = Math.max(0, ...rows.map(r => (r.hi ?? r.est)), ...(rows.map(r => r.band ? r.band : 0)));
  if (o.domain){ lo = Math.min(lo, o.domain[0]); hi = Math.max(hi, o.domain[1]); }
  const pad = (hi - lo) * 0.04; lo -= pad; hi += pad;
  const X = v => x0 + (v - lo) / (hi - lo) * (x1 - x0);
  const plotBottom = H - bottom;
  const nT = Math.max(2, Math.floor((x1 - x0) / 70)); const tk = niceTicks(lo, hi, nT); const step = tk.length > 1 ? tk[1] - tk[0] : 1;
  const gGrid = el('g', {}, svg);
  tk.forEach(t => { el('line', {x1: X(t), x2: X(t), y1: top, y2: plotBottom, stroke: C.grid}, gGrid);
    txt(gGrid, X(t), plotBottom + 16, tickFmt(t, step), {'text-anchor': 'middle', 'font-size': fs - 1}); });
  el('line', {x1: X(0), x2: X(0), y1: top, y2: plotBottom, stroke: C.ink2, 'stroke-dasharray': '4 3'}, svg);
  if (o.refLine !== undefined && o.refLine !== null) el('line', {x1: X(o.refLine), x2: X(o.refLine), y1: top, y2: plotBottom, stroke: '#111', 'stroke-dasharray': '1 3', 'stroke-width': 1.5}, svg);
  txt(svg, (x0 + x1) / 2, H - 6, o.xTitle, {'text-anchor': 'middle', 'font-size': fs, 'font-weight': 600});
  const div2 = div;
  let y = top;
  rows.forEach((r, i) => {
    if (r.sep){ y += 10; el('line', {x1: 0, x2: W, y1: y - 5, y2: y - 5, stroke: C.rule}, svg); }
    const cy = y + rowH / 2;
    const g = el('g', {class: 'mark', tabindex: 0, role: 'img', 'aria-label': r.aria || (r.label + ': ' + r.valueText)}, svg);
    el('rect', {class: 'hit', x: 0, y: y + 1, width: W, height: rowH - 2, fill: 'transparent', rx: 4}, g);
    if (r.band) el('rect', {x: X(-r.band), width: X(r.band) - X(-r.band), y: y + 6, height: rowH - 12, fill: C.mutedSoft, stroke: C.rule}, g);
    txt(g, labelW, cy + 4, r.label, {'text-anchor': 'end', 'font-size': fs, 'font-weight': r.bold ? 700 : 400, fill: r.dim ? C.muted : C.ink});
    const col = r.color || C.accent;
    if (r.lo !== undefined && r.lo !== null){
      if (r.shape === 'diamond'){
        el('polygon', {points: [X(r.lo) + ',' + cy, X(r.est) + ',' + (cy - 8), X(r.hi) + ',' + cy, X(r.est) + ',' + (cy + 8)].join(' '), fill: '#111'}, g);
      } else {
        el('line', {x1: X(r.lo), x2: X(r.hi), y1: cy, y2: cy, stroke: col, 'stroke-width': 2}, g);
        el('line', {x1: X(r.lo), x2: X(r.lo), y1: cy - 5, y2: cy + 5, stroke: col, 'stroke-width': 2}, g);
        el('line', {x1: X(r.hi), x2: X(r.hi), y1: cy - 5, y2: cy + 5, stroke: col, 'stroke-width': 2}, g);
      }
    }
    if (r.shape !== 'diamond') el(r.shape === 'circle' ? 'circle' : 'rect', r.shape === 'circle' ? {cx: X(r.est), cy: cy, r: 5.5, fill: col} : {x: X(r.est) - 5.5, y: cy - 5.5, width: 11, height: 11, fill: col}, g);
    txt(g, W - valW + 6, cy + 4, valTexts[i], {'font-size': fs, fill: r.dim ? C.muted : C.ink2, 'font-weight': r.bold ? 700 : 400});
    bindMark(g, div2, r.tip);
    y += rowH;
  });
}

/* ---------- generic horizontal bar chart (bars start at zero) ---------- */
function hbars(svgId, cats, series, o){
  const svg = document.getElementById(svgId), div = svg.parentNode; svg.innerHTML = '';
  const W = Math.max(280, div.clientWidth); const fs = W < 480 ? 12 : 13;
  const labelW = Math.max.apply(null, cats.map(c => measure(c.label, fs))) + 8;
  const barH = series.length > 1 ? 14 : 20, gap = 3, groupH = series.length * (barH + gap) + 12;
  const top = 6, bottom = 44; const H = top + cats.length * groupH + bottom;
  svg.setAttribute('viewBox', '0 0 ' + W + ' ' + H); svg.setAttribute('height', H);
  const vals = []; cats.forEach(c => series.forEach(s => vals.push(c.values[s.key])));
  const vt = cats.map(c => series.map(s => (o.fmt || (v => f(v)))(c.values[s.key])));
  const maxLab = Math.max.apply(null, vt.flat().map(t => measure(t, fs - 1))) + 8;
  let lo = Math.min(0, ...vals), hi = Math.max(0, ...vals); if (o.domain){ lo = Math.min(lo, o.domain[0]); hi = Math.max(hi, o.domain[1]); }
  const x0 = labelW + 10 + (lo < 0 ? maxLab : 0), x1 = W - maxLab - 4;
  const X = v => x0 + (v - lo) / ((hi - lo) || 1) * (x1 - x0);
  const plotBottom = H - bottom;
  const nT = Math.max(2, Math.floor((x1 - x0) / 70)); const tk = niceTicks(lo, hi, nT); const step = tk.length > 1 ? tk[1] - tk[0] : 1;
  tk.forEach(t => { el('line', {x1: X(t), x2: X(t), y1: top, y2: plotBottom, stroke: C.grid}, svg); txt(svg, X(t), plotBottom + 16, tickFmt(t, step), {'text-anchor': 'middle', 'font-size': fs - 1}); });
  el('line', {x1: X(0), x2: X(0), y1: top, y2: plotBottom, stroke: C.ink2}, svg);
  txt(svg, (x0 + x1) / 2, H - 6, o.xTitle, {'text-anchor': 'middle', 'font-size': fs, 'font-weight': 600});
  cats.forEach((c, ci) => {
    const gy = top + ci * groupH;
    txt(svg, labelW, gy + (groupH - 12) / 2 + 4, c.label, {'text-anchor': 'end', 'font-size': fs, fill: C.ink});
    series.forEach((s, si) => {
      const v = c.values[s.key]; const by = gy + si * (barH + gap);
      const g = el('g', {class: 'mark', tabindex: 0, role: 'img', 'aria-label': c.label + ', ' + s.name + ': ' + vt[ci][si]}, svg);
      el('rect', {class: 'hit', x: Math.min(X(0), X(v)) - 2, y: by - 1, width: Math.abs(X(v) - X(0)) + 4, height: barH + 2, fill: 'transparent'}, g);
      el('rect', {x: Math.min(X(0), X(v)), y: by, width: Math.max(1, Math.abs(X(v) - X(0))), height: barH, fill: s.color, rx: 2}, g);
      txt(g, v >= 0 ? X(v) + 4 : X(v) - 4, by + barH - 3, vt[ci][si], {'text-anchor': v >= 0 ? 'start' : 'end', 'font-size': fs - 1, fill: C.ink2});
      bindMark(g, div, '<b>' + esc(c.label) + '</b>' + esc(s.name) + ': ' + vt[ci][si] + (c.tips && c.tips[s.key] ? '<br>' + c.tips[s.key] : ''));
    });
  });
}

/* ---------- labels ---------- */
const BODY = { B2_PHYS: 'Physical Sciences', B2_LIFEENV: 'Life & Environment', B2_SOC: 'Social Sciences', B2_MATHDEC: 'Math & Decision',
  B3_EXP5_COHORT_2010_14: '2010–14 cohort', B4_COHORT_2015_17: '2015–17 cohort', B1_DEV: 'DEV (selection)' };
const GROUP = { 'CS+Eng': 'CS & Engineering', 'BGM+Med': 'Biochem, Genetics & Medicine', PHYS: 'Physical Sciences', LIFEENV: 'Life & Environment', SOC: 'Social Sciences', MATHDEC: 'Math & Decision Sci.' };
const FIELD = {11:'Agricultural & Biological Sci.',12:'Arts & Humanities',13:'Biochemistry, Genetics & Mol. Biol.',14:'Business, Management & Accounting',15:'Chemical Engineering',16:'Chemistry',17:'Computer Science',18:'Decision Sciences',19:'Earth & Planetary Sci.',20:'Economics, Econometrics & Finance',21:'Energy',22:'Engineering',23:'Environmental Science',24:'Immunology & Microbiology',25:'Materials Science',26:'Mathematics',27:'Medicine',28:'Neuroscience',29:'Nursing',30:'Pharmacology, Toxicology & Pharm.',31:'Physics & Astronomy',32:'Psychology',33:'Social Sciences',34:'Veterinary',35:'Dentistry',36:'Health Professions'};
const IND = { M0_density_end: 'Frontier density (period end)', D_vol_end: 'Volume-weighted field density', CONTACT_REACH: 'Contact reach', n_comm_W3: 'Community count (W3)',
  RS: 'Rao–Stirling (φmin)', G_btw: 'Gateway landing (betweenness)', log_offhome_volume: 'Log off-home volume', RETENTION_RATIO_early: 'Retention ratio', NOV: 'Novel-partner share (NOV)', ego_density_W3: 'Ego density (W3)' };
const UNIT = { PHYS: 'Physical Sciences', LIFEENV: 'Life & Environment', SOC: 'Social Sciences', MATHDEC: 'Math & Decision Sci.', COH_DEVHOME: '2010–14 cohort, DEV-home fields', COH_OTHER: '2010–14 cohort, other fields' };
const COMP = { new_edge_rate: 'New edge rate', n_comm_W3: 'Communities reached', participation: 'Participation coefficient', NOV_res: 'Novelty residual (NOV_res)', ego_density_W3: 'Ego density', edge_persistence: 'Edge persistence' };
const FEAT = { OPEN_home: 'OPEN_home', NOVCHURN_home: 'NOVCHURN_home' };
const RUNGDEF = { R0: 'R0 controls for B5 and onset year', R2: 'R2 adds contact reach, concept type, a generic-concept flag and concept level', R3: 'R3 adds the pre-onset footprint to R2' };

/* ---------- 1. headline forest ---------- */
const NONSEL = ['B2_PHYS', 'B2_LIFEENV', 'B2_SOC', 'B2_MATHDEC', 'B3_EXP5_COHORT_2010_14', 'B4_COHORT_2015_17'];
function drawFinding(){
  const feat = document.querySelector('input[name=feat]:checked').value, rung = document.querySelector('input[name=rung]:checked').value;
  const showDev = $('#f-dev').checked, showPl = $('#f-plac').checked;
  const pool = SYN.pools[feat + '|' + rung];
  const rows = [];
  let nPos = 0, nCI = 0, k = 0;
  NONSEL.forEach(b => {
    const r = SYN.rows.find(x => x.body === b && x.feature === feat); if (!r || !r[rung]) return;
    const v = r[rung]; k++; if (v.psp > 0) nPos++; if (v.ci[0] > 0) nCI++;
    const status = r.status === 'confirmatory' ? 'never used before (confirmatory)' : r.status === 'already-unsealed' ? 'outcomes read in earlier analyses' : r.status;
    rows.push({ label: BODY[b], est: v.psp, lo: v.ci[0], hi: v.ci[1], band: showPl ? r.placebo_p95 : null,
      valueText: f(v.psp) + ' ' + fci(v.ci), shortText: f(v.psp),
      tip: '<b>' + BODY[b] + '</b>Partial Spearman ' + f(v.psp) + ' ' + fci(v.ci) + '<br>n = ' + v.n.toLocaleString() + ' concepts analysed<br>' + esc(status) + '<br>Shuffled-outcome 95th pct |ρ| (R2): ' + f(r.placebo_p95, 3, false) });
  });
  rows.push({ label: 'Pooled (DL, ' + pool.k + ' bodies)', bold: true, shape: 'diamond', est: pool.est, lo: pool.ci[0], hi: pool.ci[1],
    valueText: f(pool.est) + ' ' + fci(pool.ci), shortText: f(pool.est),
    tip: '<b>DerSimonian–Laird pool</b>' + f(pool.est) + ' ' + fci(pool.ci) + '<br>I² = ' + f(pool.I2, 2, false) + ', ' + pool.sign + ' positive' });
  if (showDev){ const r = SYN.rows.find(x => x.body === 'B1_DEV' && x.feature === feat); const v = r[rung];
    rows.push({ sep: true, label: BODY.B1_DEV, dim: true, color: C.muted, est: v.psp, lo: v.ci[0], hi: v.ci[1], band: showPl ? r.placebo_p95 : null,
      valueText: f(v.psp) + ' ' + fci(v.ci), shortText: f(v.psp),
      tip: '<b>DEV selection body</b>' + f(v.psp) + ' ' + fci(v.ci) + '<br>n = ' + v.n.toLocaleString() + '. The index was chosen here, so it is not pooled.' }); }
  const xt = 'Partial Spearman with rarefied breadth, given ' + rung + ' controls';
  forest('s-forest', rows, { xTitle: xt, refLine: pool.est, domain: [-0.1, 0.3] });
  $('#bignum').textContent = f(pool.est);
  $('#bigcap').innerHTML = 'Pooled partial Spearman of ' + (feat === 'OPEN_home' ? 'OPEN<sub>home</sub>' : 'NOVCHURN<sub>home</sub>') + ' with breadth across ' + pool.k + ' non-selection bodies at rung ' + rung + ', 95% CI ' + fci(pool.ci) + '.';
  const devR = SYN.rows.find(x => x.body === 'B1_DEV' && x.feature === feat)[rung];
  let t = 'At ' + rung + ', ' + FEAT[feat].replace('_home', ' (home build)') + ' pools to ' + f(pool.est) + ' ' + fci(pool.ci) + ' over ' + pool.k + ' non-selection bodies (I² = ' + f(pool.I2, 2, false) + ', ' + pool.sign + ' positive), yet only ' + nCI + ' of ' + k + ' bodies have a CI above zero on their own.';
  if (showDev) t += ' The DEV body, where the index was chosen, gives ' + f(devR.psp) + ', ' + (devR.psp / pool.est).toFixed(2) + '× the pool.';
  if (feat === 'NOVCHURN_home') t += ' NOVCHURN was chosen on the 2015–17 cohort, so that body is excluded from its pool.';
  $('#t-finding').textContent = t;
}
document.querySelectorAll('input[name=feat],input[name=rung]').forEach(i => i.addEventListener('change', drawFinding));
$('#f-dev').addEventListener('change', drawFinding); $('#f-plac').addEventListener('change', drawFinding);

/* ---------- 2. stepper ---------- */
const P1 = CASES.pairs[0], HI = P1.members.HIGH_OPEN, LO = P1.members.LOW_OPEN;
const ZC = CASES.z_constants, COMPS = CASES.components;
function zOf(member, build, key){ const c = ZC[build][key]; const sg = COMPS.find(x => x[0] === key)[1]; return sg * (member.components[build][key] - c.mean) / c.sd; }
const STAGES = [
  { name: 'Ground and date', short: 'Ground' },
  { name: 'Popularity baseline B5', short: 'B5' },
  { name: 'Early ego network', short: 'Ego net' },
  { name: 'Score OPEN', short: 'OPEN' },
  { name: 'Follow to t0+8', short: 'Outcome' },
  { name: 'Relate across concepts', short: 'Relate' }
];
let step = 0;
function stepHTML(i){
  const b5 = m => m.B5;
  if (i === 0) return '<div class="io"><div><h4>In</h4>The 2026-09-23 OpenAlex snapshot: 476,196,327 works, 129.4 million base works 1995–2022, and 56,643 legacy concepts.</div>' +
    '<div><h4>Done</h4>Aho–Corasick title matching with stemmed verification; an LLM precision gate drops concepts with precision below 0.80. The <button class="term" data-term="t0">onset year</button> is the first year with 20 grounded publications; the <button class="term" data-term="home">home field</button> holds at least 40% of the first 30 grounded papers.</div>' +
    '<div><h4>Out</h4><strong>' + esc(HI.name) + '</strong>: t<sub>0</sub> = ' + HI.t0 + ', home ' + FIELD[HI.home] + '.<br><strong>' + esc(LO.name) + '</strong>: t<sub>0</sub> = ' + LO.t0 + ', home ' + FIELD[LO.home] + '.</div>' +
    '<div><h4>Why</h4>Every later measure is relative to the onset year and the home field, so both concepts start from the same kind of home: Engineering.</div></div>';
  if (i === 1){
    const row = (k, lab, d) => '<tr><td>' + lab + '</td><td class="n">' + f(b5(HI)[k], d, false) + '</td><td class="n">' + f(b5(LO)[k], d, false) + '</td></tr>';
    return '<div class="io"><div><h4>In</h4>Each concept\'s grounded papers from t<sub>0</sub> to t<sub>0</sub>+2.</div><div><h4>Done</h4>Compute the five <button class="term" data-term="b5">B5</button> features. The pair was matched on early volume and growth.</div></div>' +
      '<div class="tscroll"><table><caption class="sr-only">B5 baseline features</caption><thead><tr><th>B5 feature (t<sub>0</sub> to t<sub>0</sub>+2)</th><th class="n">GPU</th><th class="n">VAWT</th></tr></thead><tbody>' +
      row('logvol', 'Log early volume', 3) + row('growth_c', 'Publication growth', 3) + row('offhome_share', 'Non-home share', 3) + row('entropy', 'Shannon entropy of fields', 3) + row('reach', 'Field reach', 0) + '</tbody></table></div>' +
      '<p class="prose"><strong>Why.</strong> Popularity already predicts breadth well (B5 Spearman 0.65–0.86 across groups), and GPU is already spread wider. Any network signal must add to this baseline, which is why every result on this page is a partial correlation given B5.</p>';
  }
  if (i === 2){
    const ws = ['W1_all', 'W2_all', 'W3_all'];
    return '<div class="io"><div><h4>In</h4>The concept\'s papers in cumulative windows W1 (t<sub>0</sub>), W2 (to t<sub>0</sub>+1) and W3 (to t<sub>0</sub>+2), and the topic backbone.</div>' +
      '<div><h4>Done</h4>Build the <button class="term" data-term="ego">ego network</button>: nodes are the concept\'s positive-PMI neighbour topics, edges are backbone links between them, colours are <button class="term" data-term="leiden">Leiden communities</button>.</div></div>' +
      '<div class="chart" id="c-st"><svg id="s-st" role="group" aria-label="Topics in the ego network by window"></svg><div class="tip" role="status"></div></div>' +
      '<ul class="legend"><li><span class="sw" style="background:var(--accent)"></span>GPU (high OPEN)</li><li><span class="sw" style="background:var(--muted)"></span>VAWT (low OPEN)</li></ul>' +
      '<p class="prose"><strong>Out.</strong> By W3 GPU\'s neighbourhood has ' + HI.ego.W3_all.n_nodes + ' topics in ' + HI.ego.W3_all.n_communities + ' communities (density ' + HI.ego.W3_all.density.toFixed(2) + '); VAWT\'s has ' + LO.ego.W3_all.n_nodes + ' topics in ' + LO.ego.W3_all.n_communities + ' community (density ' + LO.ego.W3_all.density.toFixed(2) + ').</p>' +
      '<figure><img src="figures/fig_case_study_v0.png" alt="Panel a: off-home fields ever entered and retained from t0 to t0+8, GPU above VAWT throughout. Panels b and c: GPU ego network with 34 topics in 8 colour-coded communities, density 0.30; VAWT ego network with 12 topics in one Engineering community, density 0.70." width="1295" height="549" loading="lazy">' +
      '<figcaption>Matched case-study pair 1 of 7: GPU (t<sub>0</sub> = 2008, high OPEN) versus VAWT (t<sub>0</sub> = 2009, low OPEN), both with an Engineering home field and matched on early volume and growth. (a) Off-home venue fields ever entered (solid) and currently retained (dashed) from t<sub>0</sub> to t<sub>0</sub>+8. (b, c) Topic co-occurrence ego networks over t<sub>0</sub> to t<sub>0</sub>+2; node area scales with the concept\'s papers carrying the topic, colour gives the Leiden community. The pair illustrates the openness–breadth association and is not evidence for it.</figcaption></figure>';
  }
  if (i === 3){

    COMPS.forEach(([k, s]) => { rows += '<tr><td>' + COMP[k] + ' (' + (s > 0 ? '+' : MINUS) + ')</td><td class="n">' + f(HI.components.home[k], 3, false) + '</td><td class="n">' + f(zOf(HI, 'home', k)) + '</td><td class="n">' + f(LO.components.home[k], 3, false) + '</td><td class="n">' + f(zOf(LO, 'home', k)) + '</td></tr>'; });
    return '<div class="io"><div><h4>In</h4>Six measures of the home-field ego network over t<sub>0</sub> to t<sub>0</sub>+2.</div><div><h4>Done</h4>z-score each with constants frozen on all 12,499 concepts, flip the sign of ego density and edge persistence, and average: <button class="term" data-term="open">OPEN</button>.</div></div>' +
      '<div class="tscroll"><table><caption class="sr-only">OPEN components, home build</caption><thead><tr><th>Component (sign)</th><th class="n">GPU raw</th><th class="n">GPU signed z</th><th class="n">VAWT raw</th><th class="n">VAWT signed z</th></tr></thead><tbody>' + rows + '</tbody></table></div>' +
      '<div class="chart" id="c-st"><svg id="s-st" role="group" aria-label="Signed z-scores of OPEN components"></svg><div class="tip" role="status"></div></div>' +
      '<ul class="legend"><li><span class="sw" style="background:var(--accent)"></span>GPU</li><li><span class="sw" style="background:var(--muted)"></span>VAWT</li></ul>' +
      '<p class="prose"><strong>Out.</strong> OPEN<sub>home</sub> = ' + f(HI.OPEN.home) + ' for GPU and ' + f(LO.OPEN.home) + ' for VAWT (all-papers build: ' + f(HI.OPEN.all) + ' and ' + f(LO.OPEN.all) + '). You can rerun this arithmetic in <a href="#try">Try it</a>.</p>';
  }
  if (i === 4){
    return '<div class="io"><div><h4>In</h4>The concept\'s papers through t<sub>0</sub>+8.</div><div><h4>Done</h4>Count off-home fields entered and retained, and compute <button class="term" data-term="o2r">rarefied breadth</button> O<sub>2r</sub> (m = 50) over t<sub>0</sub>+6 to t<sub>0</sub>+8.</div></div>' +
      '<div class="chart" id="c-st"><svg id="s-st" role="group" aria-label="Fields entered, retained and rarefied breadth"></svg><div class="tip" role="status"></div></div>' +
      '<ul class="legend"><li><span class="sw" style="background:var(--accent)"></span>GPU</li><li><span class="sw" style="background:var(--muted)"></span>VAWT</li></ul>' +
      '<p class="prose"><strong>Why.</strong> Rarefaction separates size-adjusted breadth from sheer volume: both concepts had the same early volume, yet GPU reaches about twice as many fields in a fixed draw of 50 papers.</p>';
  }

  return '<div class="io"><div><h4>In</h4>OPEN<sub>home</sub> and O<sub>2r</sub> for every concept in a body, plus the R2 controls.</div><div><h4>Done</h4>Residualise ranks of both on the controls, correlate the residuals (<button class="term" data-term="psp">partial Spearman priority</button>), bootstrap concepts 2,000 times, then pool bodies with <button class="term" data-term="dl">DerSimonian–Laird</button>.</div>' +
    '<div><h4>Out</h4>Pooled over six non-selection bodies: <strong>' + f(pool.est) + ' ' + fci(pool.ci) + '</strong>, I² = ' + f(pool.I2, 0, false) + ', ' + pool.sign + ' positive.</div><div><h4>Why</h4>One pair is an illustration. In 7 of 7 matched pairs the high-OPEN member is broader, but only the association across thousands of concepts is evidence; see <a href="#finding">the finding</a>.</div></div>';
}
function drawStepChart(){

  } else if (step === 3){

  } else if (step === 4){

      {label: 'Retained at t0+8', values: {hi: d(HI).Bn, lo: d(LO).Bn}}, {label: 'Rarefied breadth O2r', values: {hi: oc(HI).O2r_m50, lo: oc(LO).O2r_m50}}];
    hbars('s-st', cats, ser, {xTitle: 'Off-home venue fields (count; O2r = expected fields in 50 papers)', fmt: v => Number.isInteger(v) ? String(v) : v.toFixed(2)});
  }
}
function drawPipe(){
  const svg = $('#s-pipe'); svg.innerHTML = ''; const W = Math.max(280, svg.parentNode.clientWidth); const n = STAGES.length;
  const narrow = W < 620; const H = narrow ? 56 : 78; svg.setAttribute('viewBox', '0 0 ' + W + ' ' + H); svg.setAttribute('height', H);
  const cw = W / n; const fs = 13;
  STAGES.forEach((s, i) => {
    const cx = cw * i + cw / 2, cy = 22;
    if (i < n - 1) el('line', {x1: cx + 18, x2: cx + cw - 18, y1: cy, y2: cy, stroke: C.rule, 'stroke-width': 2}, svg);
    const cur = i === step, done = i < step;
    const g = el('g', {style: 'cursor:pointer'}, svg);
    el('circle', {cx: cx, cy: cy, r: 16, fill: cur ? C.accent : done ? '#cddcee' : '#fff', stroke: cur ? C.accent : C.muted, 'stroke-width': 2}, g);
    txt(g, cx, cy + 5, String(i + 1), {'text-anchor': 'middle', 'font-size': 14, 'font-weight': 700, fill: cur ? '#fff' : C.ink2});
    if (!narrow){ const lab = measure(s.name, fs) < cw - 8 ? s.name : s.short; txt(g, cx, 62, lab, {'text-anchor': 'middle', 'font-size': fs, 'font-weight': cur ? 700 : 400, fill: cur ? C.accent : C.ink2}); }
    g.addEventListener('click', () => goStep(i));
  });
}
function goStep(i){
  step = Math.max(0, Math.min(STAGES.length - 1, i));
  document.querySelectorAll('#step-markers button').forEach((b, j) => { if (j === step) b.setAttribute('aria-current', 'step'); else b.removeAttribute('aria-current'); });
  $('#step-body').innerHTML = '<h4 style="font-size:19px">Stage ' + (step + 1) + ' of ' + STAGES.length + ': ' + STAGES[step].name + '</h4>' + stepHTML(step);
  $('#step-prev').disabled = step === 0; $('#step-next').disabled = step === STAGES.length - 1;
  $('#step-live').textContent = 'Stage ' + (step + 1) + ' of ' + STAGES.length + ': ' + STAGES[step].name;
  drawPipe(); drawStepChart(); bindTerms($('#step-body'));
}
STAGES.forEach((s, i) => { const li = document.createElement('li'); const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.textContent = (i + 1) + '. ' + s.name; b.addEventListener('click', () => goStep(i)); li.appendChild(b); $('#step-markers').appendChild(li); });
$('#step-prev').addEventListener('click', () => goStep(step - 1)); $('#step-next').addEventListener('click', () => goStep(step + 1));
$('#stepper').addEventListener('keydown', e => { if (e.target.closest('input,select,textarea')) return; if (e.key === 'ArrowLeft'){ goStep(step - 1); e.preventDefault(); } else if (e.key === 'ArrowRight'){ goStep(step + 1); e.preventDefault(); } });

function drawScreen(){

  });

'Pooled over the held-out groups, ' + nConf + ' of 10 indicators are confirmed; ' : 'In ' + UNIT[u] + ', ') + pos + ' of 10 intervals sit above zero and ' + neg + ' below. The strongest is ' + best.name + ' at ' + f(best.est) + (u === 'POOLED' ? ', but about half of that signal is a pre-onset footprint.' : '.');
}
$('#f-unit').addEventListener('change', drawScreen);

/* ---------- 3b. concept browser ---------- */
const CI = {}; COH.cols.forEach((c, i) => CI[c] = i);
const REC = COH.rows.map((r, idx) => { const o = {idx: idx}; COH.cols.forEach((c, i) => o[c] = r[i]); o.full = o.obs !== null && o.pB5 !== null && o.pB5O !== null && o.open_home !== null;
  o.excess = o.obs !== null && o.pB5 !== null ? o.obs - o.pB5 : null; o.worse = o.full ? Math.abs(o.obs - o.pB5O) > Math.abs(o.obs - o.pB5) : false; return o; });
['all'].concat(Object.keys(GROUP)).forEach(g => { const o = document.createElement('option'); o.value = g; o.textContent = g === 'all' ? 'All groups' : GROUP[g]; $('#b-group').appendChild(o); });
function spearman(x, y){ const rank = a => { const idx = a.map((v, i) => i).sort((i, j) => a[i] - a[j]); const r = new Array(a.length); let i = 0;
    while (i < idx.length){ let j = i; while (j + 1 < idx.length && a[idx[j + 1]] === a[idx[i]]) j++; for (let k = i; k <= j; k++) r[idx[k]] = (i + j) / 2 + 1; i = j + 1; } return r; };
  const rx = rank(x), ry = rank(y), n = x.length; const mx = rx.reduce((s, v) => s + v, 0) / n, my = ry.reduce((s, v) => s + v, 0) / n;
  let sxy = 0, sxx = 0, syy = 0; for (let i = 0; i < n; i++){ sxy += (rx[i] - mx) * (ry[i] - my); sxx += (rx[i] - mx) ** 2; syy += (ry[i] - my) ** 2; } return sxy / Math.sqrt(sxx * syy); }
let shown = 50, selected = null, view = [];
function filtered(){
  const q = $('#b-search').value.trim().toLowerCase(), g = $('#b-group').value, sc = $('#b-scope').value, w = $('#b-worse').checked, so = $('#b-sort').value;
  let v = REC.filter(r => (!q || r.name.toLowerCase().includes(q)) && (g === 'all' || r.group === g) && (sc === 'all' || (sc === 'obs' ? r.obs !== null : r.full)) && (!w || r.worse));
  const key = so === 'open' ? r => r.open_home : so === 'excess' ? r => r.excess : so === 'obs' ? r => r.obs : null;
  if (key) v.sort((a, b) => { const ka = key(a), kb = key(b); if (ka === null && kb === null) return a.name.localeCompare(b.name); if (ka === null) return 1; if (kb === null) return -1; return kb - ka; });
  else v.sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name));
  return v;
}
function drawBrowser(resetShown){

    b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', r === selected ? 'true' : 'false');
